title: Ex-MP Ahaja beats own relative for Tawi-Tawi 4th District parliament seat
summary: The Bangsamoro Federalist Party’s Nur-Mahadil Ahaja defeats his own relative, longtime public official Michail Ahaja

blocks.text: WINNER. Former Bangsamoro Transition Authority parliament member Nur-Mahadil Ahaja.
The Bangsamoro Federalist Party’s Nur-Mahadil Ahaja defeats his own relative, longtime public official Michail Ahaja

MANILA, Philippines – Former Bangsamoro Transition Authority parliament member Nur-Mahadil Ahaja won the Tawi-Tawi 4th District race in the first-ever Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections on Monday, September 14.

Ahaja was the bet of the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), and obtained 19,174 or 36.2% of the votes, according to Tawi-Tawi’s total certificates of canvass from the Commission on Elections’ website.
He defeated three other candidates in the 4th District race, including his own relative, independent candidate and current Tawi-Tawi provincial board member Michail Ahaja.
The losing Ahaja, who also used to be Tawi-Tawi vice governor and vice mayor of Sitangkai, placed second with 16,796 or 31.71 % of the votes.
Hot on their heels was third-placer Sanya Jamalul, daughter of the current Turtle Islands mayor and vice mayor. She ran as an independent candidate and got 16,044 or 30.29% of the votes.
The candidate of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front’s United Bangsamoro Justice Party was Mapun native Hamdan Musa Kasim. He ranked last with 946 or 1.79% of the votes.

Like other winning candidates in the BARMM polls, Ahaja will serve a special five-year transition term from October 30, 2026, to June 30, 2031. He will be one of the 32 district representatives making up 40% of the 80-seat Bangsamoro Parliament. – Rappler.com
